queries: The adaptive traffic signal system operates through an emergent collective intelligence mechanism where intersections follow simple local rules that, when combined with neighbor communication, result in system-wide optimization without explicit coordination. Each intersection follows simple local rules: if queue length is above threshold, increase green time proportionally to queue length; if throughput is below threshold, adjust offset to better match neighbor phases. These rules, combined with limited neighbor communication about phase timing, create an emergent system that self-organizes to optimize network flow. The system exhibits properties similar to slime mold network formation, where simple components create complex adaptive behavior.
sources: The Lotus Effect: Superhydrophobicity and Self-Cleaning
